 Main Card Results | UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs Nolan
 UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs Nolan Live Results, Highlights, Post-Fight Interviews With The Main Card Winners And More From Meta APEX In Las Vegas On October 31, 2026 
 By Simon Head (@simonheadsport on X)
 • Nov. 1, 2026
 The Octagon returns to Meta APEX on Halloween night to close out UFC's loaded October schedule.
 The Octagon returned to Meta APEX on Halloween night to close out UFC’s loaded October schedule, and it saw the emergence of an exciting new contender in the lightweight division.
In the main event, Australia’s Tom Nolan claimed a huge victory as he finished former lightweight title challenger and perennial contender Renato Moicano via third-round TKO, while in the co-main event, undefeated welterweight powerhouse Jacobe Smith dominated UFC vet Randy Brown to continue his rise up the 170-pound ladder.
 Main Card Results, Highlights & More: 
 More Coverage: Prelim Results | Scorecards 
 Main Event: Tom Nolan defeats Renato Moicano via TKO (punches and elbows) – Round 3, 1:28 
 In the main event of the evening, Australia’s Tom Nolan scored the biggest win of his career with a third-round TKO finish of Renato Moicano in his first UFC main event appearance.
Nolan opened up with a body kick, which Moicano checked, then answered with a big body kick of his own. The Brazilian then walked into range and, with Nolan briefly frozen, Moicano dropped levels and took Nolan to the mat.
Moicano quickly moved to Nolan’s back and went to work in search of his speciality finish, the rear-naked choke. Nolan fought his way to his feet, but Moicano stayed on his back and made Nolan carry his weight while still working for a choke.
Moicano dragged Nolan back to the canvas, but the Australian continued to fight the hands well to keep himself out of submission danger for the rest of the round.
The second round saw Nolan find his striking range as he connected with head-kick and several punches. But just as it looked like the Aussie was getting into the fight, Moicano quickly closed in and dragged Nolan to the mat.
 Moicano took Nolan’s back and locked up a body triangle, but he wasn’t able to find his way to a rear-naked choke, with Nolan’s stout defense ensuring he stayed out of danger.
Referee Dan Miragliotta surprisingly made the decision to stand the fighters back up, and Nolan immediately went to work. After finding his range, Nolan dropped Moicano and poured on a vicious barrage of strikes, then a big takedown, as he came close to finishing the Brazilian in the closing seconds of the round.
Nolan picked up where he left off at the start of Round 3 as he landed big shots on Moicano and hurt the Brazilian early in the round. Moicano turned to his grappling and took Nolan down, but Nolan immediately swept him, landed in top position, and hammered him with strikes until referee Miragliotta decided he’d seen enough and waved off the contest at the 1:28 mark.
It was a superb performance from Nolan, who claimed the biggest win of his UFC career, and announced his arrival as the latest new contender in the talent-stacked lightweight division.
 Co-Main Event: Jacobe Smith defeats Randy Brown via unanimous decision (30-26, 30-26, 30-26) 
 In the night’s co-main event, undefeated welterweight prospect Jacobe Smith took full advantage of his short-notice opportunity as he defeated Randy Brown via unanimous decision after a dominant display of wrestling and top control.
Brown quickly settled into his striking as he worked from the outside, utilizing his reach advantage and initially, Smith struggled to get into range to connect with his offense.
Eventually, Smith managed to step in and land some punishing leg kicks. Then, with 90 seconds left in the round, he charged in and drove Brown into the mat with a powerful takedown.
Smith started much quicker in Round 2 as he connected with a big leg kick, then took Brown to the canvas in the center of the Octagon. Brown tried to scoot his way to the fence, but was forced to eat some powerful ground strikes as Smith dominated from top position. A series of nasty elbows from Smith cut Brown open as he sent the veteran back to his corner at the end of the round with blood streaming down his face.

 After a cagey start to the final round, Smith timed his moment, then charged in, picked up Brown and slammed him down to the mat with a huge takedown. Brown tried in vain to find a submission off his back as Smith continued to punish him on the mat.
In the end, it was a straightforward victory for Smith, who dominated the fight on the mat through all three rounds as he earned scores of 30-26 from all three judges for a shutout victory, and the 14th win of his perfect professional career. And he did it all on just two weeks’ notice.
 Cody Durden defeats Ode’ Osbourne via unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Veteran flyweights Ode’ Osbourne and Cody Durden went head to head in a well-matched contest at 125 pounds, with Durden grinding out a unanimous decision victory off the back of his wrestling skills.
The fight hit the mat early, courtesy of a smart level change from Durden, but he had to be on his guard to avoid the threat of a guillotine choke from Osbourne. Eventually, Durden worked his neck free, then landed some solid ground and pound before taking Osbourne’s back.
Durden held Osbourne in position with a tight body triangle, and a hand-fight ensued as Osbourne tried to defend from Durden’s attempts to lock up a rear-naked choke.
Osbourne attempted to roll himself out of danger, but Durden quickly locked up a Scottish twister that appeared to have his opponent in big trouble. But, with no tap forthcoming, Durden switched to mount and battered Osbourne with ground and pound in search of a TKO finish. A stoppage looked imminent, but Osbourne swept Durden and finished the round on top as he made it back to his corner after a one-sided round.

 Osbourne started off Round 2 landing strikes, but Durden was able to drag the action to the mat again, and eventually moved himself into top position. Osbourne looked trapped, but somehow he managed to wriggle free and the action returned to the feet again, where he enjoyed some success in the stand-up before the round came to a close.
The third round played out almost exclusively on the mat, with Osbourne riding Durden’s back, but unable to work his way into position to set up a fight-winning choke. In the end, the best he could muster was some punches from off his back to close out the matchup.
Ultimately, Durden’s wrestling superiority through Rounds 1 and 2 proved crucial as he ran out the unanimous decision winner, with scores of 29-28 across the board.

 Luana Santos defeats Yana Santos via unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 
 In the battle of bantamweight namesakes, Luana Santos did just enough to edge out Yana Santos on the scorecards after a grapple-heavy contest went all three rounds.
The pair immediately clinched up in the opening seconds of Round 1, with Luana looking to set up a judo throw to take the action to the mat, while Yana looked to use the clinch to score with her Muay Thai knees and elbows.
With Yana effectively nullifying Luana’s judo attack and keeping things standing, the Russian was able to score with short-range strikes. But, after a period of inactivity, referee Chris Tognioni ordered the pair to break and return to the center of the Octagon. That put the fight in Yana’s wheelhouse as she connected with strikes from range before Lyana closed in and initiated another clinch. However, she wasn’t able to make anything of it as time ran out at the end of the round.
Round 2 began with Luana looking to strike, but her punches kept falling short as Yana managed the range expertly, and countered with shots of her own. But things improved for Luana when she surged into range and took Yana to the canvas.

 Luana took Yana’s back as she attempted to get into position to attack a rear-naked choke, but Yana responded with punches over her shoulder to keep Luana at bay, then eventually worked her way free. But it was only a temporary reprieve, as Luana managed to take Yana to the mat in the closing seconds of the round to seal a much improved round for the Brazilian.
It set up a crucial final round, and Luana managed to trip Yana to the mat early, then she took the Russian’s back as she established a strong position with three and a half minutes left in the round.
Yana continually punched Luana to the face with no-look punches over her own shoulder, while also trying to defend from Luana’s choke attempts. But she couldn’t shake off her opponent as Luana continued to ride Yana like a backpack for the remainder of the round to take the fight all the way to the final horn.
After all three rounds were completed, the judges scored the bout 29-28 to Luana, who extended her win streak to four with the 12th victory of her career.

 Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani defeats Farman Hasanov via TKO (doctor stoppage) – Round 3, 2:11 
 The opening bout of the main card delivered a thrilling scrap as welterweight Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani outbattled undefeated Farman Hasanov en route to a third-round doctor-stoppage TKO victory.
Lebosnoyani had to work off the back foot early as Hasanov pushed the pace in the opening exchanges, but as the opening round wore on, “JPL” established his striking and started to score consistently with body kicks and counter punches as Hasanov stepped in.
Both men traded powerful high kicks, but it was Lebosnoyani’s strikes that were more accurate as he continued to chip away at Hasanov’s gas tank with body kicks. And, in the closing seconds of the round, the Las Vegas native stood and traded with Hasanov, and consistently got the better of him as he finished the round strongly.
Hasanov came out for Round 2 looking to wrestle, but despite executing an early takedown, Lebosnoyani immediately bounced back to his feet and gained separation. Lebosnoyani was eating punches from Hasanov, but his work was cleaner, more varied, and more successful.

 Lebosnoyani kept stabbing at Hasanov’s body with his front kick, and as the round progressed, Hasanov started to tire. And with the Azerbaijani fighter slowing down, Lebosnoyani turned up the heat and hurt his opponent with punches and kicks as he poured on the pressure in a wild final exchange at the end of the round.
After two thrilling rounds, Lebosnoyani started the final round as he finished the first, by pushing forward and throwing punches. And with Hasanov cut across almost the entirety of his left eyelid, referee Dan Miragliotta paused the fight for the Octagonside physician to inspect the damage.
The official’s intervention was proved correct, with the doctor recommending the fight be stopped, as Lebosnoyani sealed the first stoppage victory of his UFC career to take his UFC record to 3-0, and his career record to 12-2.
